text: damn ok now the one question i have, shouldnt my performance change drastically from when like lets say my camera view looks like this: [Image #6] versus this: [Image #7] because it genuinely doesnt move the needle between the two, which i have to feel is another area for performance gains
resolution: User measured identical fps looking at 143M tris of foliage vs looking at empty ground — correct diagnosis, and the code confirmed it: the draw walk's only cull was distance-based AND explicitly skipped instanced batches (3d.zig 'an instance batch carries many positions'), so the five whole-world foliage family batches submitted every triangle every frame regardless of camera. Built chunk-granular frustum culling: regenPaintFoliage records one {row range, bounding sphere} segment per chunk per family (rows are already chunk-contiguous from the walk), a new scene3d_instance_segments field carries them, and the static draw path extracts Gribb-Hartmann frustum planes from the vp and draws only surviving segments, coalescing adjacent visible ranges into single draws. Segmentless batches draw whole (unchanged); shadow staging is a separate loop, untouched. Commit 040223366; needs rebuild. Verification signal for the user: after rebuild, the HUD TRI counter should crater when looking away from the painted area, and fps should rise correspondingly at high paint densities.
